summary_rationale: 1. Mode A neutral baseline exhibited complete 20/20 FALSE_POSITIVE class collapse (5.0% 3-class accuracy, 0.0% TP recall), violating explicit anti-benign-assumption rules.

2. Mode B policy guidance raised raw 3-class accuracy from 5% to only 10% (2/20, McNemar p=1.0), triggered 6/9 false missing-command-line hallucinations on CrowdStrike, misclassified the sole FP as TP, and achieved 0/10 abstentions on inconclusive Prisma SASE alerts.

3. Prompt engineering or minor rule tuning cannot reliably overcome a quantized 7B model that fails basic instruction adherence (claims present JSON fields are missing), basic network topology (calls 3.109.76.166 internal and 172.25.14.67 external), and path reading (calls Program Files a writable temp path).

4. Deterministic validator architecture (Mode C) proved highly valuable as a safety firewall—raising 3-class agreement to 45% (McNemar p=0.0156 vs Mode B), blocking 8/10 ungrounded Prisma decisive calls and 1/1 FP-as-TP misclassification, and reducing missed-TP-as-FP from 9/9 (Mode A) to 0/9—justifying retention of Verdictum AI's pipeline while upgrading the underlying LLM (e.g., 14B/32B+ non-AWQ or unquantized/stronger model) AND fixing the mismatched Prisma SASE policy template.
